Inspect the supplied codebase and identify its core component: the connected set of responsibilities around which the application's main behavior and state are organized. Generate a single ASCII tree diagram showing that core component's call structure: the main operations it performs and which activations invoke which. Choose the scope and level of detail that best explain the codebase. Ground the diagram in the source code.

Structure the tree as a call decomposition of the core component:
  - Top-level branches are the core's main operations: the entry points or recurring loops through which its behavior happens. Each operation appears in exactly one place; when another flow re-enters it, reference it by name.
  - Depth always means "is invoked during": a child is a call made by, or a step performed within, its parent activation. List siblings in execution order.
  - Show synchronous calls and asynchronous hand-offs (queues, events, workers, timers) distinctly. Show decisions as sibling branches under the step that makes them, and loops once with their exit condition.
  - Other relationships appear only as brief -> lines where they change the flow; do not organize the tree around modules or owners.
Cover breadth before depth:
  - Name every main operation of the core, even in one line, before tracing any of them.
  - When a call triggers a substantial flow of its own, give it a child line naming that flow's phases, even if you do not expand them.
  - Do not trace one operation down to individual helper calls while another main operation remains a single line.

Here is the "3+1" model of conceptual codebase models:
1. [REPLACED] Containment	      where code lives
2. [REPLACED] Lexical scope	    which names code can see
  -> *collapse* into 1. Modular structure
    I want to collapse Containment / Lexical scope into a single category, called modular structure, which:
    - abstracts out the source file level organization
      - but retains boundaries and visibility: what a component exposes versus keeps internal
    - retains dependency graph
    - groups components into higher level, logic-semantical categorizations
3. Call (dynamic)     which activation invoked which
4. Ownership          responsibility for state, storage, resources, and their lifetimes: who creates, retains, changes, or releases them
1. [SPECIAL] Data dependency   is a different kind of thing. It isn’t a fifth organizational choice; it is the record of what actually needs what for the program to compute its result. It’s a graph, and it exists before you decide how to organize anything.

Keep the following in mind when generating your diagram:
  - there should be 60/40 between code refs and nat lang

Few-shot examples (synthetic style references, not source facts):
Example 1: Incremental compiler
Incremental compiler -- reuse follows the module dependency graph
|
|-- [M] BuildGraph connects source modules to their compilation artifacts
|   |-- modules[moduleId]: ModuleUnit
|   |   |-- sourceHash -> immutable source bytes
|   |   |-- imports[] -> resolved module identities
|   |   `-- interfaceHash -> names and types visible to consumers
|   `-- units[unitId]: AnalysisUnit
|       |-- mutually dependent modules share one unit
|       `-- dependencies[] -> units whose interfaces must be available first
|
|-- [C] compileUnit(unitId) resolves one reusable result
|   |-- [D] member source hashes + dependency interfaces + compiler options
|   |   `-- analysisKey, including the compiler implementation version
|   |-- ArtifactCache.lookup(analysisKey)
|   |   |-- Hit -> recover typed modules and diagnostics
|   |   `-- Miss -> analyze the unit
|   |       |-- [C] Parser.parse(source) -> syntax with source spans
|   |       |-- [C] Binder.bind(syntax, dependencyInterfaces)
|   |       |   `-- Scope
|   |       |       |-- declarations[name] -> local Symbol
|   |       |       |-- parent -> enclosing lexical scope
|   |       |       `-- exports -> symbols visible across the module boundary
|   |       `-- [C] TypeChecker.check(boundUnit) -> typed modules + diagnostics
|   `-- Successful analysis -> Emitter.emit(typedModules, target)
|       |-- [D] typed modules + target version + emission options -> objectKey
|       `-- ObjectArtifact
|           |-- object code / exported interface / source map
|           `-- [O] ArtifactCache retains complete immutable entries
|               `-- consumers borrow artifacts; eviction follows cache policy
|
|-- [C] rebuild(changedPaths) propagates only relevant changes
|   |-- Capture new source hashes and resolve changed imports
|   |   `-- [D] updated graph -> regroup cycles and order affected units
|   |-- Reanalyze affected units
|   |   |-- Exported interface changed -> invalidate dependent analysis keys
|   |   `-- Interface unchanged -> consumers can reuse their typed modules
|   `-- [D] reachable object hashes + runtime + linker options -> bundleKey
|       `-- Linker.link(objects) produces the executable bundle
|           `-- changed implementation can require linking without retyping consumers
|
`-- [O] BuildScheduler controls transient execution
    |-- ready queue -> units whose dependency results are available
    |   `-- independent units may run concurrently
    |-- running[unitId] -> task + worker lease
    |   |-- [C] invoke compileUnit(unitId)
    |   `-- task settlement returns the worker lease
    |-- cancel(buildId)
    |   `-- stop scheduling -> signal tasks -> await settlement -> release snapshot
    `-- BuildResult retains bundle references and source-located diagnostics
        `-- [D] diagnostic spans + captured sources -> stable reported locations

Example 2: Telemetry ingestion service
Telemetry ingestion service
|
|-- [M] IngestGateway accepts batches from device connections
|   |-- accept(connection, envelope): BatchReceipt
|   |   |-- [D] credentials + device registry -> authorized tenant/device
|   |   `-- [C] decode -> validate envelope -> PartitionRouter.route(batch)
|   |       |-- Partition key = tenantId + deviceId
|   |       `-- One device's batches reach the same ordered partition
|   |-- [O] Retains connection state until disconnect
|   |   |-- pending[batchId] -> receipt waiter
|   |   `-- socket close detaches waiters; accepted work can still finish
|   `-- Admission limit
|       |-- available capacity -> enqueue batch
|       `-- full partition queue -> return retryable rejection
|
|-- [O] PartitionWorker owns one partition's ingestion progress
|   |-- Retained state
|   |   |-- queue: BoundedQueue<AcceptedBatch>
|   |   |   `-- accepted batches wait here before processing
|   |   |-- checkpoint: PartitionCheckpoint
|   |   |   |-- partitionId / committedOffset
|   |   |   `-- lastSequence[deviceId] -> latest committed device sequence
|   |   `-- lease: PartitionLease
|   |       |-- ownerId / epoch / expiresAt
|   |       `-- [D] current epoch -> authority to commit new progress
|   |
|   |-- [C] run() drains the queue one batch at a time
|   |   `-- process(batch)
|   |       |-- Establish batch identity
|   |       |   |-- key = tenantId + deviceId + batchId
|   |       |   `-- [C] EventStore.lookupReceipt(key)
|   |       |       |-- Same payload hash -> return committed receipt
|   |       |       |-- Different payload hash -> reject identity conflict
|   |       |       `-- Missing receipt -> prepare a new commit
|   |       |
|   |       |-- Normalize measurements
|   |       |   `-- [C] SchemaRegistry.resolve(batch.schemaVersion)
|   |       |       |-- [M] Exposes versioned field and unit definitions
|   |       |       `-- [D] raw samples + exact schema -> Measurement[]
|   |       |           |-- identity: tenantId / deviceId / sequence
|   |       |           |-- observation: timestamp / metric / value / unit
|   |       |           `-- provenance: batchId / schemaVersion / payloadHash
|   |       |
|   |       |-- Check sequence continuity
|   |       |   |-- [D] firstSequence + checkpoint.lastSequence[deviceId]
|   |       |   |   `-- next expected sequence or a detected gap
|   |       |   |-- Contiguous -> stage measurements
|   |       |   `-- Gap or overlap -> reject without advancing checkpoint
|   |       |
|   |       `-- Commit and acknowledge
|   |           |-- [C] EventStore.commit(batch, checkpoint, lease.epoch)
|   |           |   |-- [D] measurements + batch identity + next checkpoint
|   |           |   |   `-- one durable transaction
|   |           |   `-- Stale lease epoch -> reject the former owner
|   |           `-- After confirmed commit
|   |               |-- Install returned checkpoint
|   |               `-- Resolve gateway waiters with BatchReceipt
|   |                   `-- receipt confirms storage, not downstream indexing
|   |
|   `-- Lease loss or shutdown
|       |-- [C] Stop admission and stop dequeuing new work
|       |-- In-flight commit may have an uncertain outcome
|       |   `-- retry resolves through its durable batch receipt
|       `-- [O] Release queue entries and detach remaining waiters
|           `-- next owner restores progress from EventStore
|
|-- [M] EventStore binds stored events to durable progress
|   |-- [M] Exposes commit / lookupReceipt / restoreCheckpoint / scan
|   |-- Internal transaction
|   |   |-- Verify current partition lease epoch
|   |   |-- Append measurements with partition offsets
|   |   |-- Insert receipt under the unique batch identity
|   |   `-- Advance PartitionCheckpoint in the same commit
|   |       `-- failure rolls back events, receipt and checkpoint together
|   |-- [O] Retains the durable event log and retry receipts
|   |   |-- worker restarts leave both intact
|   |   `-- receipt retention defines the supported retry horizon
|   `-- scan(partitionId, afterOffset): EventPage
|       `-- [D] committed log + cursor -> ordered events and next cursor
|
`-- [M] ProjectionHost maintains independently rebuildable read models
    |-- [O] consumers[name]: ProjectionConsumer
    |   |-- cursor[partitionId] -> last applied event offset
    |   |-- handler: ProjectionHandler
    |   `-- cancellation + poll subscription
    |
    |-- Registered consumers
    |   |-- LatestReading
    |   |   |-- [D] device/metric + sequence -> newest accepted value
    |   |   `-- older replayed events cannot replace a newer reading
    |   `-- HourlySummary
    |       |-- [D] metric + observation timestamp -> aggregation bucket
    |       `-- count / sum / minimum / maximum
    |           `-- late observations update their original time bucket
    |
    |-- [C] poll() -> EventStore.scan() -> handler.apply(page)
    |   `-- Projection transaction
    |       |-- Apply only offsets beyond the stored consumer cursor
    |       `-- Save changed rows and cursor atomically
    |           `-- crash before commit -> safely read the same page again
    |
    `-- rebuild(name, newVersion)
        |-- [O] Create separate projection tables and fresh cursors
        |-- [C] Replay retained events while the current version serves reads
        `-- [D] rebuilt cursors + captured log positions -> readiness
            `-- switch readers after catch-up; retire the previous tables

Use the examples as a varied pool of representational choices. Let the supplied evidence determine depth, branching, density, and relationship types; do not copy their domain facts, exact shapes, counts, or require every tag.

Tree validation: Start with one root title, followed by a connector-only line. Place all other content beneath explicit branches. Do not insert annotations, references, legends, or explanatory text between the root title and its first branch.

Root title
|
|-- First component
|   `-- Supporting detail
`-- Second component

Before returning, verify that every branch belongs to the single root.

Return a JSON object with exactly one field, "ascii", containing the diagram string. Return exactly one ASCII tree with one root, printable ASCII characters, spaces and LF newlines. No Markdown fences or surrounding prose. The complete tree must fit within 20000 characters. Do not add separate side diagrams.

{"ascii":"Ghostty core: Surface terminal session -- input, PTY execution, terminal state and rendering
|
|-- Surface.init(): create a session (src/Surface.zig:477)
|   |-- Config.changeConditionalState(); DerivedConfig.init(); read runtime DPI and size
|   |-- app.font_grid_set.ref(); initialize shared render device; Renderer.init()
|   |-- Allocate renderer_state.mutex; initialize renderer.Thread and termio.Thread
|   |-- Exec.init(); Termio.init(): configure command/environment, terminal grid and VT stream
|   |   `-- renderer_state.terminal -> io.terminal; parsing and frame snapshots share its mutex
|   |-- rt_app.performAction(.cell_size, .size_limit); call resize() below
|   |-- [async spawn] renderer.Thread.threadMain() -> rendering loop below
|   |-- [async spawn] termio.Thread.threadMain() -> IO control loop below
|   `-- recomputeInitialSize(); report configured title; clear app.first
|
|-- Surface.keyCallback(): handle a key event (src/Surface.zig:2792)
|   |-- Apply modifier remaps; prepare optional inspector recording
|   |-- maybeHandleBinding(): resolve key tables, sequences and binding flags
|   |   |-- Binding matched -> call performBindingAction() below; consumed events return
|   |   `-- Not consumed -> continue terminal input processing
|   |-- Check disable_keyboard; update mouse/modifier state; remember pressed_key
|   |-- encodeKey(): use terminal keyboard modes to construct a write request
|   |   |-- No encoded bytes -> return .ignored
|   |   |-- Child already exited -> discard request; call close() below
|   |   `-- Otherwise -> call queueIo() below with .write_small/.write_stable/.write_alloc
|   `-- For non-modifier input: clear selection as configured; scroll viewport; queueRender()
|       `-- [async wake] -> rendering loop below; deferred inspector recording runs on return
|
|-- Text and IME event entry points (src/Surface.zig:2669,3426)
|   |-- On textCallback(text): call completeClipboardPaste(text, true) below
|   `-- On preeditCallback(text): lock terminal state; clear selection/prior preedit
|       |-- Decode UTF-8 into display-width-aware codepoints; install or clear preedit
|       `-- Mark preedit dirty; queueRender() [async wake] -> rendering loop below
|
|-- Pointer event entry points: select, scroll or report to the application
|   |-- On mouseButtonCallback(): update click/modifier state (src/Surface.zig:3918)
|   |   `-- Evaluate button, capture mode and selection gesture
|   |       |-- Application capture -> mouseReport(); call queueIo() below
|   |       |-- Local selection -> selection_gesture.press/release(); setSelection()/setSelectionAndCopy()
|   |       |-- Link or prompt click -> processLinks()/maybePromptClick(); open URL or send cursor movement
|   |       `-- Paste gesture -> call startClipboardRequest() below
|   |-- On cursorPosCallback()/mousePressureCallback() (src/Surface.zig:4614,4678)
|   |   |-- Update position/link hover; report motion or extend/deep-press selection
|   |   |-- Drag beyond viewport -> queueIo(.selection_scroll) [async] -> IO selection timer below
|   |   `-- setSelection(); queueRender() [async wake] -> rendering loop below
|   `-- On scrollCallback(): normalize wheel/pixel deltas; lock terminal state (src/Surface.zig:3584)
|       `-- Choose scrolling behavior from active screen and mouse modes
|           |-- Alternate screen + alternate-scroll, without reporting -> queue cursor-key writes
|           |-- Mouse reporting -> mouseReport() for each wheel step; call queueIo() below
|           `-- Otherwise -> Terminal.scrollViewport(); queueRender() [async wake]
|
|-- Surface.performBindingAction(): execute a resolved command (src/Surface.zig:4941)
|   `-- Dispatch by action scope and tag
|       |-- App/window/tab/split action -> App.performAction()/newWindow() or rt_app.performAction()
|       |   `-- Runtime performs GUI changes; newly created terminal widgets enter Surface.init()
|       |-- Text/CSI/ESC/cursor-key action -> encode bytes; call queueIo(); scroll to bottom
|       |-- Reset/clear/scroll/prompt action -> mutate locked terminal state or queue IO control message
|       |-- Font action -> call setFontSize() below
|       |-- Copy/paste action -> copySelectionToClipboards() or call startClipboardRequest() below
|       |-- Search action -> show search UI; lazily initialize search state and spawn search.Thread
|       |   |-- [async mailbox] .change_needle/.select -> search loop below
|       |   `-- Empty query/end_search -> stop and join search; notify runtime
|       |-- Inspector action -> rt_app.performAction(.inspector) -> inspector entry points below
|       `-- Close action -> call close() below or delegate window/tab closure to runtime
|
|-- Clipboard request/completion entry points (src/Surface.zig:6017,6167,6219)
|   |-- On startClipboardRequest(): inspect paste-event mode and clipboard access policy
|   |   |-- Denied OSC 52 read -> return .unsupported
|   |   `-- Allowed -> rt_surface.clipboardRequest(); request text, MIME listing or protocol data
|   |       `-- [runtime completion event] -> completeClipboardRequest() below
|   |-- On completeClipboardRequest(): dispatch request kind
|   |   |-- Ordinary paste -> call completeClipboardPaste() below
|   |   |-- Paste-event listing -> terminal.paste.paste(); call queueIo() with encoded event
|   |   |-- OSC 52/Kitty read -> authorize; encode protocol response; call queueIo()
|   |   `-- OSC 52/Kitty write -> authorize; rt_surface.setClipboard(); send protocol status if needed
|   |-- completeClipboardPaste(): snapshot terminal paste modes (src/Surface.zig:6264)
|   |   |-- Unsafe and not confirmed -> return error.UnsafePaste; runtime may request confirmation
|   |   `-- Allowed -> scrollToBottom(); input.paste.encode(); queueIo() for each nonempty segment
|   `-- On denyClipboardRequest(): finish denial handling and release protocol request state
|
|-- Size/font entry points: reconcile pixels, cells and PTY dimensions
|   |-- On sizeCallback(): ignore unchanged screen size; otherwise call resize() (src/Surface.zig:2600)
|   |-- On contentScaleCallback(): update DPI-sensitive font/padding state (src/Surface.zig:3765)
|   |   `-- Call setFontSize() below; recompute initial sizing
|   |-- setFontSize(): acquire shared font grid; setCellSize() (src/Surface.zig:2510,2536)
|   |   |-- setCellSize() -> call resize() below; report new cell size to runtime
|   |   `-- [async mailbox] .font_grid -> renderer installs grid and releases old reference
|   `-- resize(): save screen size; balance padding; calculate grid size (src/Surface.zig:2618)
|       |-- call queueIo(.resize) [async] -> IO coalescing timer below
|       `-- [async mailbox + wake] renderer .resize -> setScreenSize(); rendering loop below
|
|-- Surface.updateConfig(): reload session configuration (src/Surface.zig:1804)
|   |-- Apply conditional state; derive replacement config
|   |   |-- Derivation fails -> retain current config and return
|   |   `-- Success -> replace config; restore mouse visibility if needed
|   |-- endKeySequence(); deactivateAllKeyTables(); call setFontSize() above
|   |   `-- Preserve manually adjusted font size; otherwise use new configured size
|   |-- Derive independent renderer and Termio configs
|   |-- [async mailbox] renderer .change_config; queueIo(.change_config) -> respective loops below
|   `-- queueRender(); rt_app.performAction(.set_title/.config_change)
|       `-- Termio.changeConfig() updates emulator policy/colors, not the running command or cwd
|
|-- Focus, visibility and display callbacks: adapt session activity
|   |-- On focusCallback(): App.focusSurface(); ignore unchanged focus (src/Surface.zig:3466)
|   |   |-- [async mailbox] renderer .focus
|   |   |-- If losing focus -> synthesize releases by re-entering keyCallback()
|   |   `-- queueRender(); showMouse(); update terminal focus; queueIo(.focused)
|   |-- On occlusionCallback(): ignore unchanged visibility (src/Surface.zig:3437)
|   |   |-- Update terminal visibility; queueIo(.visibility_report) if enabled
|   |   `-- [async mailbox + wake] renderer .visible -> rendering loop below
|   |-- On displayRealized()/displayUnrealized() (src/Surface.zig:2584)
|   |   `-- Notify renderer; unrealize wakes render thread to release GPU resources
|   |-- On refreshCallback(): queueRender() [async wake] -> rendering loop below (src/Surface.zig:3554)
|   |-- On draw(): call Renderer.drawFrame(true) below for synchronous presentation (src/Surface.zig:925)
